## 2026 Aviation Scholarships for U.S. High School Students:

### PILOTS:

- 1 – **$20,000 [Captain Judy Rice](https://epicflightacademy.com/captain-judy-rice/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any of our [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 12 – **$5,000 Pilot Scholarships** for Flight Training (to be awarded at each of our flight training [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 1 – **$5,000 [King Air Nation](https://kingairnation.com/blog/taking-flight-with-king-air-nation-foundation-82a6c2/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any campus)

### MECHANICS:

- 2 – **$20,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at [CVG Airport](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations-erlanger/) and [New Smyrna Beach](https://epicflightacademy.com/aircraft-mechanic/))
- 2- **$10,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at CVG Airport and New Smyrna Beach)

The student who wins this award must show exemplary dedication in the spirit of Captain Judy! **This scholarship can be used at any of our campuses.**

## High School Scholarship Requirements

- First, the **applicant must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident**.
- Furthermore, the applicant must currently be a junior or senior attending high school in the U.S. for the flight training scholarships.
- For the aircraft mechanic scholarship, applicants must currently be a senior attending high school in the U.S.
- Applicants must be turning 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026 (flight training); or, you must be 18 years old by time of completing program (aircraft mechanic)
- All applicants must be able to start training within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.
- Also, you must be able to use the scholarship within 24 months.
- Additionally, you must have parent or guardian’s approval if under 18 years of age.
- Most importantly, applicants must have consistent, reliable transportation to attend Epic Flight Academy or be willing to relocate to your respective campus during training.
- Finally, you must be able to present a [Third Class Medical](https://epicflightacademy.com/flight-school-faq/what-exams-are-required-to-get-my-private-pilot-rating-and-where-do-i-take-them/) for the flight training scholarship.

### DEADLINE TO SUBMIT APPLICATION WAS OCTOBER 1, 2026

### What is included in your application?

- **Upload PDF document containing Community Service Involvement & Extracurricular Activities**, including Organization/Affiliation, Date and Duration, and Location (for pilots only)
- **Upload PDF document containing responses to both of the following Short Essay prompts**:
  - Short Essay 1: What personal attributes would you look for in a scholarship applicant? (for pilots only)
  - Short Essay 2: What is your motivation for your aviation training? (Include your goals.)
- **Upload 2 Letters of Recommendation:** At least one must be from a high school teacher, counselor, coach, or other school official. Both Letters of Recommendation may be from teachers, counselors, coaches, or other school officials. Letters of Recommendation must not be from anyone related to you, including a guardian. Letters of Recommendation should be from adults who have served in a supervisory role to you. Please ensure that the Letters of Recommendation include the reference’s contact information.
- **Create YouTube Video:** In two minutes or less, explain why you feel that you are the strongest candidate to receive a scholarship. Upload the video to YouTube, and be prepared to provide the link in the application.
- **Upload Aviation-Related Photo:** Provide us with an aviation-related photo of yourself in either jpg, jpeg, or png file format. If you win, we will share your photo on our website and in other scholarship materials.

## How to Apply

Scholarship applications have closed for 2026.

## Scholarship FAQs

**How many scholarships will be awarded in 2026?** We will award 14 pilot scholarships and 4 aircraft mechanic scholarships to eligible high school students.

**What is included in the high school scholarship application?** The application consists of:

- two short essay questions (pilot app only)
- your current high school information (both pilot and mechanic apps)
- community service (pilot only)
- letters of recommendation (both pilot and mechanic)
- one video uploaded to YouTube (both pilot and mechanic)
- one photo (both pilot and mechanic)

**Do I get additional points for submitting my application earlier that other applicants?** The date an application is received carries no weight in the scoring process. However, the application must be submitted by the **October 1st deadline**.

**When will I know if I’ve been selected for the final round?** We will notify finalists by October 28th.

**What is the next step if I’m chosen for the final round?** Final round applicants participate in a phone interview with a panel of judges who will determine the scholarship recipients. .

**Must I attend the award ceremony?** If you win, you are not required to attend, although we do hope you will. Our aviation scholarship awards event is a lot of fun, and you’ll get to meet a lot of Epic staff and students.

**Will I get additional points for visiting Epic Flight Academy?** Applicants that visit Epic Flight Academy do not receive any additional points or consideration in the scoring process.

## 2026 Aviation Scholarships for U.S. High School Students:

### PILOTS:

- 1 – **$20,000 [Captain Judy Rice](https://epicflightacademy.com/captain-judy-rice/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any of our [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 12 – **$5,000 Pilot Scholarships** for Flight Training (to be awarded at each of our flight training [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 1 – **$5,000 [King Air Nation](https://kingairnation.com/blog/taking-flight-with-king-air-nation-foundation-82a6c2/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any campus)

### MECHANICS:

- 2 – **$20,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at [CVG Airport](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations-erlanger/) and [New Smyrna Beach](https://epicflightacademy.com/aircraft-mechanic/))
- 2- **$10,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at CVG Airport and New Smyrna Beach)

The student who wins this award must show exemplary dedication in the spirit of Captain Judy! **This scholarship can be used at any of our campuses.**

## High School Scholarship Requirements

- First, the **applicant must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident**.
- Furthermore, the applicant must currently be a junior or senior attending high school in the U.S. for the flight training scholarships.
- For the aircraft mechanic scholarship, applicants must currently be a senior attending high school in the U.S.
- Applicants must be turning 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026 (flight training); or, you must be 18 years old by time of completing program (aircraft mechanic)
- All applicants must be able to start training within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.
- Also, you must be able to use the scholarship within 24 months.
- Additionally, you must have parent or guardian’s approval if under 18 years of age.
- Most importantly, applicants must have consistent, reliable transportation to attend Epic Flight Academy or be willing to relocate to your respective campus during training.
- Finally, you must be able to present a [Third Class Medical](https://epicflightacademy.com/flight-school-faq/what-exams-are-required-to-get-my-private-pilot-rating-and-where-do-i-take-them/) for the flight training scholarship.

### DEADLINE TO SUBMIT APPLICATION WAS OCTOBER 1, 2026

### What is included in your application?

- **Upload PDF document containing Community Service Involvement & Extracurricular Activities**, including Organization/Affiliation, Date and Duration, and Location (for pilots only)
- **Upload PDF document containing responses to both of the following Short Essay prompts**:
  - Short Essay 1: What personal attributes would you look for in a scholarship applicant? (for pilots only)
  - Short Essay 2: What is your motivation for your aviation training? (Include your goals.)
- **Upload 2 Letters of Recommendation:** At least one must be from a high school teacher, counselor, coach, or other school official. Both Letters of Recommendation may be from teachers, counselors, coaches, or other school officials. Letters of Recommendation must not be from anyone related to you, including a guardian. Letters of Recommendation should be from adults who have served in a supervisory role to you. Please ensure that the Letters of Recommendation include the reference’s contact information.
- **Create YouTube Video:** In two minutes or less, explain why you feel that you are the strongest candidate to receive a scholarship. Upload the video to YouTube, and be prepared to provide the link in the application.
- **Upload Aviation-Related Photo:** Provide us with an aviation-related photo of yourself in either jpg, jpeg, or png file format. If you win, we will share your photo on our website and in other scholarship materials.

## How to Apply

Scholarship applications have closed for 2026.

## Scholarship FAQs

**How many scholarships will be awarded in 2026?** We will award 14 pilot scholarships and 4 aircraft mechanic scholarships to eligible high school students.

**What is included in the high school scholarship application?** The application consists of:

- two short essay questions (pilot app only)
- your current high school information (both pilot and mechanic apps)
- community service (pilot only)
- letters of recommendation (both pilot and mechanic)
- one video uploaded to YouTube (both pilot and mechanic)
- one photo (both pilot and mechanic)

**Do I get additional points for submitting my application earlier that other applicants?** The date an application is received carries no weight in the scoring process. However, the application must be submitted by the **October 1st deadline**.

**When will I know if I’ve been selected for the final round?** We will notify finalists by October 28th.

**What is the next step if I’m chosen for the final round?** Final round applicants participate in a phone interview with a panel of judges who will determine the scholarship recipients. .

**Must I attend the award ceremony?** If you win, you are not required to attend, although we do hope you will. Our aviation scholarship awards event is a lot of fun, and you’ll get to meet a lot of Epic staff and students.

**Will I get additional points for visiting Epic Flight Academy?** Applicants that visit Epic Flight Academy do not receive any additional points or consideration in the scoring process.

- 12 – **$5,000 Pilot Scholarships** for Flight Training (to be awarded at each of our flight training [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 1 – **$5,000 [King Air Nation](https://kingairnation.com/blog/taking-flight-with-king-air-nation-foundation-82a6c2/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any campus)

### MECHANICS:

- 2 – **$20,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at [CVG Airport](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations-erlanger/) and [New Smyrna Beach](https://epicflightacademy.com/aircraft-mechanic/))
- 2- **$10,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at CVG Airport and New Smyrna Beach)

- Applicants must be turning 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026 (flight training); or, you must be 18 years old by time of completing program (aircraft mechanic)
- All applicants must be able to start training within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.

- Additionally, you must have parent or guardian’s approval if under 18 years of age.

## 2026 Aviation Scholarships for U.S. High School Students:

### PILOTS:

- 1 – **$20,000 [Captain Judy Rice](https://epicflightacademy.com/captain-judy-rice/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any of our [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 12 – **$5,000 Pilot Scholarships** for Flight Training (to be awarded at each of our flight training [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 1 – **$5,000 [King Air Nation](https://kingairnation.com/blog/taking-flight-with-king-air-nation-foundation-82a6c2/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any campus)

### MECHANICS:

- 2 – **$20,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at [CVG Airport](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations-erlanger/) and [New Smyrna Beach](https://epicflightacademy.com/aircraft-mechanic/))
- 2- **$10,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at CVG Airport and New Smyrna Beach)

The student who wins this award must show exemplary dedication in the spirit of Captain Judy! **This scholarship can be used at any of our campuses.**

## High School Scholarship Requirements

- First, the **applicant must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident**.
- Furthermore, the applicant must currently be a junior or senior attending high school in the U.S. for the flight training scholarships.
- For the aircraft mechanic scholarship, applicants must currently be a senior attending high school in the U.S.
- Applicants must be turning 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026 (flight training); or, you must be 18 years old by time of completing program (aircraft mechanic)
- All applicants must be able to start training within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.
- Also, you must be able to use the scholarship within 24 months.
- Additionally, you must have parent or guardian’s approval if under 18 years of age.
- Most importantly, applicants must have consistent, reliable transportation to attend Epic Flight Academy or be willing to relocate to your respective campus during training.
- Finally, you must be able to present a [Third Class Medical](https://epicflightacademy.com/flight-school-faq/what-exams-are-required-to-get-my-private-pilot-rating-and-where-do-i-take-them/) for the flight training scholarship.

### DEADLINE TO SUBMIT APPLICATION WAS OCTOBER 1, 2026

### What is included in your application?

- **Upload PDF document containing Community Service Involvement & Extracurricular Activities**, including Organization/Affiliation, Date and Duration, and Location (for pilots only)
- **Upload PDF document containing responses to both of the following Short Essay prompts**:
  - Short Essay 1: What personal attributes would you look for in a scholarship applicant? (for pilots only)
  - Short Essay 2: What is your motivation for your aviation training? (Include your goals.)
- **Upload 2 Letters of Recommendation:** At least one must be from a high school teacher, counselor, coach, or other school official. Both Letters of Recommendation may be from teachers, counselors, coaches, or other school officials. Letters of Recommendation must not be from anyone related to you, including a guardian. Letters of Recommendation should be from adults who have served in a supervisory role to you. Please ensure that the Letters of Recommendation include the reference’s contact information.
- **Create YouTube Video:** In two minutes or less, explain why you feel that you are the strongest candidate to receive a scholarship. Upload the video to YouTube, and be prepared to provide the link in the application.
- **Upload Aviation-Related Photo:** Provide us with an aviation-related photo of yourself in either jpg, jpeg, or png file format. If you win, we will share your photo on our website and in other scholarship materials.

## How to Apply

Scholarship applications have closed for 2026.

## Scholarship FAQs

**How many scholarships will be awarded in 2026?** We will award 14 pilot scholarships and 4 aircraft mechanic scholarships to eligible high school students.

**What is included in the high school scholarship application?** The application consists of:

- two short essay questions (pilot app only)
- your current high school information (both pilot and mechanic apps)
- community service (pilot only)
- letters of recommendation (both pilot and mechanic)
- one video uploaded to YouTube (both pilot and mechanic)
- one photo (both pilot and mechanic)

**Do I get additional points for submitting my application earlier that other applicants?** The date an application is received carries no weight in the scoring process. However, the application must be submitted by the **October 1st deadline**.

**When will I know if I’ve been selected for the final round?** We will notify finalists by October 28th.

**What is the next step if I’m chosen for the final round?** Final round applicants participate in a phone interview with a panel of judges who will determine the scholarship recipients. .

**Must I attend the award ceremony?** If you win, you are not required to attend, although we do hope you will. Our aviation scholarship awards event is a lot of fun, and you’ll get to meet a lot of Epic staff and students.

**Will I get additional points for visiting Epic Flight Academy?** Applicants that visit Epic Flight Academy do not receive any additional points or consideration in the scoring process.

- 1 – **$20,000 [Captain Judy Rice](https://epicflightacademy.com/captain-judy-rice/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any of our [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 12 – **$5,000 Pilot Scholarships** for Flight Training (to be awarded at each of our flight training [campuses](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations/))
- 1 – **$5,000 [King Air Nation](https://kingairnation.com/blog/taking-flight-with-king-air-nation-foundation-82a6c2/) Pilot Scholarship** for Flight Training (can be used at any campus)

### MECHANICS:

- 2 – **$20,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at [CVG Airport](https://epicflightacademy.com/locations-erlanger/) and [New Smyrna Beach](https://epicflightacademy.com/aircraft-mechanic/))
- 2- **$10,000 Aircraft Mechanic Scholarships** for Aircraft Mechanics (One each at CVG Airport and New Smyrna Beach)

The student who wins this award must show exemplary dedication in the spirit of Captain Judy! **This scholarship can be used at any of our campuses.**

## High School Scholarship Requirements

- First, the **applicant must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident**.
- Furthermore, the applicant must currently be a junior or senior attending high school in the U.S. for the flight training scholarships.
- For the aircraft mechanic scholarship, applicants must currently be a senior attending high school in the U.S.
- Applicants must be turning 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026 (flight training); or, you must be 18 years old by time of completing program (aircraft mechanic)
- All applicants must be able to start training within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.
- Also, you must be able to use the scholarship within 24 months.
- Additionally, you must have parent or guardian’s approval if under 18 years of age.
- Most importantly, applicants must have consistent, reliable transportation to attend Epic Flight Academy or be willing to relocate to your respective campus during training.
- Finally, you must be able to present a [Third Class Medical](https://epicflightacademy.com/flight-school-faq/what-exams-are-required-to-get-my-private-pilot-rating-and-where-do-i-take-them/) for the flight training scholarship.

### DEADLINE TO SUBMIT APPLICATION WAS OCTOBER 1, 2026

### What is included in your application?

- **Upload PDF document containing Community Service Involvement & Extracurricular Activities**, including Organization/Affiliation, Date and Duration, and Location (for pilots only)
- **Upload PDF document containing responses to both of the following Short Essay prompts**:
  - Short Essay 1: What personal attributes would you look for in a scholarship applicant? (for pilots only)
  - Short Essay 2: What is your motivation for your aviation training? (Include your goals.)
- **Upload 2 Letters of Recommendation:** At least one must be from a high school teacher, counselor, coach, or other school official. Both Letters of Recommendation may be from teachers, counselors, coaches, or other school officials. Letters of Recommendation must not be from anyone related to you, including a guardian. Letters of Recommendation should be from adults who have served in a supervisory role to you. Please ensure that the Letters of Recommendation include the reference’s contact information.
- **Create YouTube Video:** In two minutes or less, explain why you feel that you are the strongest candidate to receive a scholarship. Upload the video to YouTube, and be prepared to provide the link in the application.
- **Upload Aviation-Related Photo:** Provide us with an aviation-related photo of yourself in either jpg, jpeg, or png file format. If you win, we will share your photo on our website and in other scholarship materials.

## How to Apply

Scholarship applications have closed for 2026.

**How many scholarships will be awarded in 2026?** We will award 14 pilot scholarships and 4 aircraft mechanic scholarships to eligible high school students.

**What is included in the high school scholarship application?** The application consists of:

- two short essay questions (pilot app only)
- your current high school information (both pilot and mechanic apps)
- community service (pilot only)
- letters of recommendation (both pilot and mechanic)
- one video uploaded to YouTube (both pilot and mechanic)
- one photo (both pilot and mechanic)

**When will I know if I’ve been selected for the final round?** We will notify finalists by October 28th.

**What is the next step if I’m chosen for the final round?** Final round applicants participate in a phone interview with a panel of judges who will determine the scholarship recipients. .

**Must I attend the award ceremony?** If you win, you are not required to attend, although we do hope you will. Our aviation scholarship awards event is a lot of fun, and you’ll get to meet a lot of Epic staff and students.

**Will I get additional points for visiting Epic Flight Academy?** Applicants that visit Epic Flight Academy do not receive any additional points or consideration in the scoring process.

### AVTRIP Scholarship: $2,000

### PURPOSE

Avfuel Corporation of Ann Arbor, Michigan, has established funds available for the purpose of furthering aviation education. These funds will be distributed under the name of the “AVTRIP Scholarship”.

#### The AVTRIP Scholarship

The AVTRIP Scholarship was designed to award one current AVTRIP member with funds to use toward furthering his or her aviation education. The scholarship will be in the amount of $2,000. These funds may be used for, but not limited to, the following areas: flight training, educational tuition fees, and a new license or rating.

A maximum of one AVTRIP Scholarship will be awarded for each calendar year.

[APPLY](https://form.jotform.com/260607434083151)

### APPLICATION DEADLINE

Complete applications will be due by **11:59 p.m. EDT on October 31st, 2026.**

### SELECTION CRITERIA

Avfuel Corporation will make the selection of the awarded recipients based solely on the answers of the application packet. Semi-finalists may be invited to a personal interview by staff of Avfuel Corporation and industry representatives who will make the final selection. The scholarship recipients will be notified by Avfuel.

### PAYMENT OF SCHOLARSHIPS

The scholarships will be distributed by check. The check will be made payable to the recipient and the educational institution of the recipient’s choice. The check must be endorsed by both, and must be used for the purposes of furthering the recipient’s aviation education. The 2026 scholarships must be redeemed by October 31, 2027.

Recipients must provide Avfuel Corporation with a detailed description of how the funds will be used.

$1,500, $1,000, $500

### PURPOSE

Avfuel Corporation of Ann Arbor, Michigan, has established funds available for the purpose of furthering aviation education. These funds will be distributed under the name of the “Avfuel Pilot-in-Training Scholarship”.

#### The Avfuel Pilot-in-Training Scholarship

The Avfuel Pilot-in-Training Scholarship was designed to award three students with funds to use toward furthering their aviation education. The scholarship will be in the amounts of $1,500, $1,000 and $500. These funds may be used for, but not limited to, the following areas: flight training, educational tuition fees, and a new license.

A maximum of three AVTRIP Pilot-in-Training Scholarships will be awarded for each calendar year.

Avfuel reserves the right to not award any scholarship in a given year if no sufficient application is received.

[APPLY](https://form.jotform.com/253366200193148)

### APPLICATION DEADLINE

Complete applications will be due by **11:59 p.m. EDT on October 31st, 2026**.

### SELECTION CRITERIA

Avfuel Corporation will make the selection of the awarded recipients based solely on the answers of the application packet. Semi-finalists may be invited to a personal interview by staff of Avfuel Corporation and industry representatives who will make the final selection. The scholarship recipients will be notified by Avfuel.

### PAYMENT OF SCHOLARSHIPS

The scholarships will be distributed by check. The check will be made payable to the recipient and the educational institution of the recipient’s choice. The check must be endorsed by both, and must be used for the purposes of furthering the recipient’s aviation education. The 2026 scholarships must be redeemed by October 31, 2027.

Recipients must provide Avfuel Corporation with a detailed description of how the funds will be used.

evidence.excerpt: While completing the application, applicants will be asked to:

Account verification is necessary for any student who creates an account on the NHS website and can be completed by any NHS member at your school as soon as they are inducted. We recommend that students create accounts and get them verified by the adviser as early as possible so that they receive updates from the NHS national office. Verification allows the adviser to confirm membership of these students so that they can access these member-exclusive benefits and communications, including access to the NHS Scholarship. Students cannot log into the NHS Scholarship until they are verified.

If a verified NHS student decides to apply for the NHS Scholarship, they must enter the NHS Adviser Certification request into the scholarship platform. This allows the adviser to provide feedback on the individual student, including up-to-date reflections on standing and contributions to the school and chapter, which are not part of the basic account verification process.

# The Honors College Presidential Scholarship

### The 2027 Presidential Scholarship is now **_open_**. It will close _**December 1, 2026**_ at midnight MST.

Presidential Scholarships are Montana State University's most distinguished academic
awards, recognizing scholastic achievement, demonstrated leadership, and unique personal
qualities. Scholarship recipients receive annual tuition waivers, a generous stipend,
and priority registration. Recent Presidential Scholars have gone on to receive renowned
awards such as the Goldwater, Truman, Rhodes, Marshall and Mitchell scholarships.
As ambassadors of the university, they reflect its highest ideals through demonstrated
leadership, public service, and academic excellence.  Montana residents and non residents
are eligible.

The Presidential Scholarship is a rigorous, competitive application, doubling as your
application to the Honors College at Montana State University. Recipients of the scholarship
routinely have a 3.9 non-weighted GPA or higher and are ranked in the top 3% of their
class.

Please review our [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html) to determine if you are a competitive candidate for the scholarship.

All students interested in the Presidential Scholarship must complete the [MSU application](https://www.montana.edu/admissions/apply/) and be accepted to the university before completing the Presidential Scholarship
Application.

[Apply for the Presidential Scholarship](https://montana.academicworks.com/opportunities/30968)

### Eligibility Requirements

- Incoming freshman, first-time, first-year student
- High school non-weighted GPA of 3.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale


  - If you do not have a 3.7+ GPA, but feel you would be competitive for this scholarship,
     please contact the Honors College office at [contact redacted].
- Acceptance to MSU

### How To Apply

1. [Apply](https://www.montana.edu/admissions/apply/) and be accepted to MSU.
2. Claim your [NetID](https://www3.montana.edu/netidclaim/).
3. _Sign in_ to the [Cat$cholarships portal](https://montana.academicworks.com/) (gold button on the upper right corner of the screen).
4. Submit the General Scholarships Application _as soon as possible_. This must be complete to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship.
5. Access the Presidential Scholarship application and contact your recommenders.

1. Talk to one (1) high school counselor and two (2) recommenders. **_It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure that all materials, including letters_**
      **_or recommendation, are recieved by the deadline._**
2. Input the emails of the high school counselor and two recommenders into the Cat$cholarships
       portal and press "save". This sends your recommenders a link to complete their portion
       of the application.
3.  You can review your reference submissions under the recommendation tab on the Cat$cholarships
       portal home.
6. Complete the Presidential Scholarship Application. Return to complete or update the
    General Scholarships Application.
7. The portal will shut off at **_midnight Mountain Standard Time_**. Do _not_ wait until the last minute to submit.

### Selection Criteria

- Honors College Alignment
- Academic Excellence
- Leadership and Service

### Recommender Information

It is the responsibility of the student to ensure letters of recommendation are received
by the December 1st deadline. Transcripts and letters of recommendation will _not_ be accepted by mail or email. They **must** be uploaded to the Cat$cholarship application portal via the personal links counselors
and recommenders receive by email. Please check your spam before contacting our office.

### Scholarship Renewal

Presidential Scholars must maintain a 3.7 MSU GPA and complete an average of 16 MSU
credits per semester (32 MSU credits per year). Presidential Scholarships are renewable
for up to eight (8) academic semesters (excluding summer terms). Early graduation
results in forfeiting of unused semesters.

Any student applying to college for the first time with a 3.7 unweighted GPA (or higher)
is encouraged to apply for the Presidential Scholarship.  This includes out-of-state,
international, and homeschool students.

# Presidential Scholarship FAQ

## [What is the Presidential Scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e122)

The "Presidential" is the most prestigious scholarship awarded by our university and
includes a full tuition waiver as well as a generous stipend renewable for four years.
As many as 24 Presidential Scholarships may be awarded. Finalists who do not receive
the Presidential Scholarship will be considered for the Provost Scholarship, which
also includes a full tuition waiver and a stipend renewable for four years.

## [Who can apply to the scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e127)

Any student applying to college for the first time with a 3.7 unweighted GPA (or higher)
is encouraged to apply for the Presidential Scholarship.  This includes out-of-state,
international, and homeschool students.

## [What are my chances of receiving this scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e132)

In 2026, we reviewed 1,216 completed applications and awarded 22 Presidential Scholarships
and 1 Provost Scholarship. Approximately 1 in 53 applicants received a Presidential
or Provost scholarship that year.

## [When will I hear if I've received the scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e137)

In early February, students with completed applications will be notified of their
Honors College admission decision and finalist status. Finalists will be invited to
interview virtually in the last week of February. Decisions will be made soon after
that. All scholarship decisions will be communicated by email.

## [Is the selection based on ACT/SAT scores?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e142)

No. ACT/SAT scores are no longer required for the Presidential Scholarship application
and are not taken into account for the award decisions.

## [Does the size of my high school matter?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e147)

No. The size (number of students) of the applicant's high school is not a statistical
indicator of success for these awards. The selection committee recognizes that applicants
from smaller schools may not have all the opportunities available to students at larger
schools.

## [Are home-schooled applicants accommodated?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e152)

Yes. Home-schooled students have historically been successful in this competition
at a rate similar to public or private school applicants, but should call us for recommendations
on how to best represent themselves using the standard application process.

## [Is my high school GPA important?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e157)

Yes. Your high school GPA is important, but is one of several criteria considered
by the selection committee. The diagram below is from the 2026 application class.
Most of the awardees had a reported GPA of 4.00, but a few students were awarded a
scholarship with less than a 4.00 GPA.

[image omitted]

## [What about GPA weighting with AP or Honors courses?]([redacted locator])

The diagram above represents the _reported_ GPAs, which may or may not have been weighted. Furthermore, high schools assign GPA
points and weigh courses in a variety of ways. Based on your transcript, we will calculate
a non-weighted GPA. We will also consider the number of credits earned eligible for
both high school and college credit, AP, IB high level, or dual credit courses.

## [If applications are due in December, how are my senior-year grades considered?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e174)

These grades will not be taken into consideration, unless your quarter/trimester/semester
ends prior to you submitting your application. The majority of our applicants will
report grades from only the 9th, 10th, and 11th years because at the time of submitting
the application they have not completed the first 12th year grading cycle.

## [What if my high school does not provide class ranking information?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e179)

Some indication of class standing is important to us. **If your school does not rank students, please ask your school counselor to provide**
**a confidential or percentile ranking (for example, top 1%, top 5%, etc.) as part of**
**the counselor recommendation. This information will only be available to the review**
**committee; it will not be visible to applicants.**

## [If I am awarded a scholarship, what are the rules for renewal?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e186)

Presidential Scholars must complete 32 credit hours per academic year and maintain
a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5. Provost Scholars must complete 30 credit hours per
academic year and maintain a 3.3 cumulative GPA. Both Presidential and Provost Scholars
must be continuously enrolled as full-time students and are expected to be active
members of the Honors College.

## [How much are these scholarships worth?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e191)

Using Fall 2025/Spring 2026 tuition costs, the four-year value of a Presidential Scholarship
exceeds $42,000 for Montana residents and $140,000 for non-residents. The Provost
Scholarship exceeds $30,000 for Montana residents and $128,000 for non-residents.
Both scholarships cover tuition, but not fees. the Presidential Scholarship includes
a $4,000 stipend (shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including
room and board. Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned
to the student as a cash award. The Provost Scholarship includes a $1,000 stipend
(shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including room and board.
Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned to the student
as a cash award. Please note that our university has a freshman housing requirement.

## [Are all finalists guaranteed either a Presidential or Provost Scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e196)

No. It is possible that some finalists (those invited to interview) may not be selected
for either scholarship.

## [Do I need to also apply to the Honors College?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e201)

No. Your Presidential Scholarship application will serve as your application to the
Honors College. We will notify you of your status when we make interview invitations
in early February.

## [If offered a scholarship, may I defer my award?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e206)

No. A Presidential or Provost Scholarship may not be deferred. If you intend to accept
the scholarship, you must enroll at Montana State University in the fall of 2027.

## [What is the application process?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e211)

1\. You must first apply to MSU and be admitted. You will need your [Net ID](https://www3.montana.edu/netidclaim/) (an MSU ID assigned to you upon admission) to proceed with the Presidential Scholarship
application process.

2\. Begin and submit the general scholarship application in [Cat $cholarships](https://montana.academicworks.com/). You will be able to edit the contents of the general application after submission,
so you can submit it before completing the application. You will not gain access to
the supplemental questions for the Presidential Scholarship until your general application
has been submitted.

3\. **When you gain access to the Presidential Scholarship application, scroll to the bottom**
**of the application and input the names and emails of your counselor and recommenders**
**first.** Once you save that information, your recommenders will receive an email from our
system that prompts them to complete their recommendations. We recommend that you
check with your references to make sure they received the emails that prompt them
to complete their recommendations. If they didn't receive the link, you can resend
it through the "References" tab in Cat Scholarships. Please contact the Honors College
if they still don't receive the link.

4\. The submission deadline for student's materials is **December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, Mountain Daylight Time**. Please note that technical assistance will only be available until 5 PM, MDT, on
that day, so we strongly encourage applicants to submit their applications early so
technical glitches may be addressed. Late submissions will not be accepted for any
reason, including time zone miscalculations and technical glitches after 5 PM, MDT.

5\. It is the **applicant's responsibility** to ensure that their counselor and recommenders have submitted their materials by
December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, MST.

## [Do I need to be committed to Montana State to apply?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e237)

No. Only students who are offered and accept the scholarship are committed to MSU.
The application itself is not binding.

# The Honors College Presidential Scholarship

### The 2027 Presidential Scholarship is now **_open_**. It will close _**December 1, 2026**_ at midnight MST.

Presidential Scholarships are Montana State University's most distinguished academic
awards, recognizing scholastic achievement, demonstrated leadership, and unique personal
qualities. Scholarship recipients receive annual tuition waivers, a generous stipend,
and priority registration. Recent Presidential Scholars have gone on to receive renowned
awards such as the Goldwater, Truman, Rhodes, Marshall and Mitchell scholarships.
As ambassadors of the university, they reflect its highest ideals through demonstrated
leadership, public service, and academic excellence.  Montana residents and non residents
are eligible.

The Presidential Scholarship is a rigorous, competitive application, doubling as your
application to the Honors College at Montana State University. Recipients of the scholarship
routinely have a 3.9 non-weighted GPA or higher and are ranked in the top 3% of their
class.

Please review our [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html) to determine if you are a competitive candidate for the scholarship.

All students interested in the Presidential Scholarship must complete the [MSU application](https://www.montana.edu/admissions/apply/) and be accepted to the university before completing the Presidential Scholarship
Application.

[Apply for the Presidential Scholarship](https://montana.academicworks.com/opportunities/30968)

### Eligibility Requirements

- Incoming freshman, first-time, first-year student
- High school non-weighted GPA of 3.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale


  - If you do not have a 3.7+ GPA, but feel you would be competitive for this scholarship,
     please contact the Honors College office at [contact redacted].
- Acceptance to MSU

### How To Apply

1. [Apply](https://www.montana.edu/admissions/apply/) and be accepted to MSU.
2. Claim your [NetID](https://www3.montana.edu/netidclaim/).
3. _Sign in_ to the [Cat$cholarships portal](https://montana.academicworks.com/) (gold button on the upper right corner of the screen).
4. Submit the General Scholarships Application _as soon as possible_. This must be complete to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship.
5. Access the Presidential Scholarship application and contact your recommenders.

1. Talk to one (1) high school counselor and two (2) recommenders. **_It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure that all materials, including letters_**
      **_or recommendation, are recieved by the deadline._**
2. Input the emails of the high school counselor and two recommenders into the Cat$cholarships
       portal and press "save". This sends your recommenders a link to complete their portion
       of the application.
3.  You can review your reference submissions under the recommendation tab on the Cat$cholarships
       portal home.
6. Complete the Presidential Scholarship Application. Return to complete or update the
    General Scholarships Application.
7. The portal will shut off at **_midnight Mountain Standard Time_**. Do _not_ wait until the last minute to submit.

### Selection Criteria

- Honors College Alignment
- Academic Excellence
- Leadership and Service

### Recommender Information

It is the responsibility of the student to ensure letters of recommendation are received
by the December 1st deadline. Transcripts and letters of recommendation will _not_ be accepted by mail or email. They **must** be uploaded to the Cat$cholarship application portal via the personal links counselors
and recommenders receive by email. Please check your spam before contacting our office.

### Scholarship Renewal

Presidential Scholars must maintain a 3.7 MSU GPA and complete an average of 16 MSU
credits per semester (32 MSU credits per year). Presidential Scholarships are renewable
for up to eight (8) academic semesters (excluding summer terms). Early graduation
results in forfeiting of unused semesters.

# Presidential Scholarship FAQ

## [What is the Presidential Scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e122)

The "Presidential" is the most prestigious scholarship awarded by our university and
includes a full tuition waiver as well as a generous stipend renewable for four years.
As many as 24 Presidential Scholarships may be awarded. Finalists who do not receive
the Presidential Scholarship will be considered for the Provost Scholarship, which
also includes a full tuition waiver and a stipend renewable for four years.

## [Who can apply to the scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e127)

Any student applying to college for the first time with a 3.7 unweighted GPA (or higher)
is encouraged to apply for the Presidential Scholarship.  This includes out-of-state,
international, and homeschool students.

## [What are my chances of receiving this scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e132)

In 2026, we reviewed 1,216 completed applications and awarded 22 Presidential Scholarships
and 1 Provost Scholarship. Approximately 1 in 53 applicants received a Presidential
or Provost scholarship that year.

## [When will I hear if I've received the scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e137)

In early February, students with completed applications will be notified of their
Honors College admission decision and finalist status. Finalists will be invited to
interview virtually in the last week of February. Decisions will be made soon after
that. All scholarship decisions will be communicated by email.

## [Is the selection based on ACT/SAT scores?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e142)

No. ACT/SAT scores are no longer required for the Presidential Scholarship application
and are not taken into account for the award decisions.

## [Does the size of my high school matter?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e147)

No. The size (number of students) of the applicant's high school is not a statistical
indicator of success for these awards. The selection committee recognizes that applicants
from smaller schools may not have all the opportunities available to students at larger
schools.

## [Are home-schooled applicants accommodated?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e152)

Yes. Home-schooled students have historically been successful in this competition
at a rate similar to public or private school applicants, but should call us for recommendations
on how to best represent themselves using the standard application process.

## [Is my high school GPA important?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e157)

Yes. Your high school GPA is important, but is one of several criteria considered
by the selection committee. The diagram below is from the 2026 application class.
Most of the awardees had a reported GPA of 4.00, but a few students were awarded a
scholarship with less than a 4.00 GPA.

[image omitted]

## [What about GPA weighting with AP or Honors courses?]([redacted locator])

The diagram above represents the _reported_ GPAs, which may or may not have been weighted. Furthermore, high schools assign GPA
points and weigh courses in a variety of ways. Based on your transcript, we will calculate
a non-weighted GPA. We will also consider the number of credits earned eligible for
both high school and college credit, AP, IB high level, or dual credit courses.

## [If applications are due in December, how are my senior-year grades considered?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e174)

These grades will not be taken into consideration, unless your quarter/trimester/semester
ends prior to you submitting your application. The majority of our applicants will
report grades from only the 9th, 10th, and 11th years because at the time of submitting
the application they have not completed the first 12th year grading cycle.

## [What if my high school does not provide class ranking information?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e179)

Some indication of class standing is important to us. **If your school does not rank students, please ask your school counselor to provide**
**a confidential or percentile ranking (for example, top 1%, top 5%, etc.) as part of**
**the counselor recommendation. This information will only be available to the review**
**committee; it will not be visible to applicants.**

## [If I am awarded a scholarship, what are the rules for renewal?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e186)

Presidential Scholars must complete 32 credit hours per academic year and maintain
a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5. Provost Scholars must complete 30 credit hours per
academic year and maintain a 3.3 cumulative GPA. Both Presidential and Provost Scholars
must be continuously enrolled as full-time students and are expected to be active
members of the Honors College.

## [How much are these scholarships worth?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e191)

Using Fall 2025/Spring 2026 tuition costs, the four-year value of a Presidential Scholarship
exceeds $42,000 for Montana residents and $140,000 for non-residents. The Provost
Scholarship exceeds $30,000 for Montana residents and $128,000 for non-residents.
Both scholarships cover tuition, but not fees. the Presidential Scholarship includes
a $4,000 stipend (shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including
room and board. Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned
to the student as a cash award. The Provost Scholarship includes a $1,000 stipend
(shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including room and board.
Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned to the student
as a cash award. Please note that our university has a freshman housing requirement.

## [Are all finalists guaranteed either a Presidential or Provost Scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e196)

No. It is possible that some finalists (those invited to interview) may not be selected
for either scholarship.

## [Do I need to also apply to the Honors College?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e201)

No. Your Presidential Scholarship application will serve as your application to the
Honors College. We will notify you of your status when we make interview invitations
in early February.

## [If offered a scholarship, may I defer my award?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e206)

No. A Presidential or Provost Scholarship may not be deferred. If you intend to accept
the scholarship, you must enroll at Montana State University in the fall of 2027.

## [What is the application process?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e211)

1\. You must first apply to MSU and be admitted. You will need your [Net ID](https://www3.montana.edu/netidclaim/) (an MSU ID assigned to you upon admission) to proceed with the Presidential Scholarship
application process.

2\. Begin and submit the general scholarship application in [Cat $cholarships](https://montana.academicworks.com/). You will be able to edit the contents of the general application after submission,
so you can submit it before completing the application. You will not gain access to
the supplemental questions for the Presidential Scholarship until your general application
has been submitted.

3\. **When you gain access to the Presidential Scholarship application, scroll to the bottom**
**of the application and input the names and emails of your counselor and recommenders**
**first.** Once you save that information, your recommenders will receive an email from our
system that prompts them to complete their recommendations. We recommend that you
check with your references to make sure they received the emails that prompt them
to complete their recommendations. If they didn't receive the link, you can resend
it through the "References" tab in Cat Scholarships. Please contact the Honors College
if they still don't receive the link.

4\. The submission deadline for student's materials is **December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, Mountain Daylight Time**. Please note that technical assistance will only be available until 5 PM, MDT, on
that day, so we strongly encourage applicants to submit their applications early so
technical glitches may be addressed. Late submissions will not be accepted for any
reason, including time zone miscalculations and technical glitches after 5 PM, MDT.

5\. It is the **applicant's responsibility** to ensure that their counselor and recommenders have submitted their materials by
December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, MST.

## [Do I need to be committed to Montana State to apply?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e237)

No. Only students who are offered and accept the scholarship are committed to MSU.
The application itself is not binding.

a $4,000 stipend (shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including
room and board. Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned
to the student as a cash award. The Provost Scholarship includes a $1,000 stipend
(shown in the value above), which is first applied to fees, including room and board.
Any remaining amount after such fees have been deducted will be returned to the student
as a cash award. Please note that our university has a freshman housing requirement.

## [Are all finalists guaranteed either a Presidential or Provost Scholarship?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e196)

No. It is possible that some finalists (those invited to interview) may not be selected
for either scholarship.

## [Do I need to also apply to the Honors College?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e201)

No. Your Presidential Scholarship application will serve as your application to the
Honors College. We will notify you of your status when we make interview invitations
in early February.

## [If offered a scholarship, may I defer my award?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e206)

No. A Presidential or Provost Scholarship may not be deferred. If you intend to accept
the scholarship, you must enroll at Montana State University in the fall of 2027.

## [What is the application process?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e211)

1\. You must first apply to MSU and be admitted. You will need your [Net ID](https://www3.montana.edu/netidclaim/) (an MSU ID assigned to you upon admission) to proceed with the Presidential Scholarship
application process.

2\. Begin and submit the general scholarship application in [Cat $cholarships](https://montana.academicworks.com/). You will be able to edit the contents of the general application after submission,
so you can submit it before completing the application. You will not gain access to
the supplemental questions for the Presidential Scholarship until your general application
has been submitted.

3\. **When you gain access to the Presidential Scholarship application, scroll to the bottom**
**of the application and input the names and emails of your counselor and recommenders**
**first.** Once you save that information, your recommenders will receive an email from our
system that prompts them to complete their recommendations. We recommend that you
check with your references to make sure they received the emails that prompt them
to complete their recommendations. If they didn't receive the link, you can resend
it through the "References" tab in Cat Scholarships. Please contact the Honors College
if they still don't receive the link.

4\. The submission deadline for student's materials is **December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, Mountain Daylight Time**. Please note that technical assistance will only be available until 5 PM, MDT, on
that day, so we strongly encourage applicants to submit their applications early so
technical glitches may be addressed. Late submissions will not be accepted for any
reason, including time zone miscalculations and technical glitches after 5 PM, MDT.

5\. It is the **applicant's responsibility** to ensure that their counselor and recommenders have submitted their materials by
December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM, MST.

## [Do I need to be committed to Montana State to apply?](https://www.montana.edu/honors/scholarships_faq.html\#collapsed84e108_d84e237)

No. Only students who are offered and accept the scholarship are committed to MSU.
The application itself is not binding.

## Tips For a Winning Essay

1

### No AI Writing

All entries are checked with AI detection tools. Essays flagged as AI-generated are disqualified with no exceptions.

2

### Proofread Carefully

Check for typos and grammar issues. Not everything gets underlined in red in your editor.

Common Questions

## Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible to apply?
+

Any U.S. citizen currently enrolled or planning to enroll in an accredited U.S. college,
university, or trade school during the upcoming academic year. This includes undergraduate,
graduate, and trade school students.


How much is the award?
+

One $2,500 award, paid directly to the winner by mailed check.
No purchase is necessary to apply or win.


Can I use AI to write my essay?
+

No. Every essay is checked with AI content detection tools.
Any submission flagged as AI-generated is disqualified.
The essay must be entirely your own work.


What is the application deadline?
+

Applications close on December 31, 2026.
The winner is selected and announced in January 2027.


Do I need to follow KCK on social media?
+

Yes, following Kitchen Cabinet Kings on at least 2 social media platforms is required to enter.
You choose which platforms. Links to all our profiles are on this page.
You will enter your username(s) in the application form to confirm.


How is the winner chosen?
+

Both founders read every essay personally. The winner is chosen based on the quality,
originality, and strength of their argument.
All decisions are at the sole discretion of Kitchen Cabinet Kings.


What format does my essay need to be in?
+

Submit your essay as a PDF or .doc file through the application form on this page.
Maximum 500 words.


Can a previous winner apply again?
+

No. This is a one-time scholarship per person. Prior recipients are not eligible to reapply.


## Terms & Conditions

1\. Eligibility and Privacy
+

Kitchen Cabinets Online, LLC (d/b/a "Kitchen Cabinet Kings") is committed to safeguarding your privacy. By using this site or submitting an entry, you consent to the collection, use, storage, and disclosure of your information as outlined in our [Privacy Policy](https://kitchencabinetkings.com/privacy-policy.html).

**Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled, or planning to enroll, in an accredited U.S. college, university, or trade school program during the upcoming academic year.**

# MUS Honor Scholarship

## General Information

The MUS Honor Scholarship (MUSHS) is a 4-year renewable scholarship, which waives
the recipient’s tuition when used at an eligible campus. Its average value at a 4-year
Montana campus is $5,000 a year or $20,000 for four years. The scholarship does not
cover mandatory or class fees. Students should ask the college for a list of fees
that are not covered by the scholarship. The Board of Regents intends to offer up
to 200 scholarships (contingent upon continued funding of the program) annually. This scholarship will be awarded in accordance with the [MUSHS Eligibility and Criteria Procedures](https://mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/MUS_Honor_Scholarship-Eligibility_and_Procedures.pdf).

[View the MUSHS Fact Sheet](https://mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/MUSHS-Fact-Sheet%202024.pdf)

[Access the MUSHS FAQ Page](https://awardmontana.mus.edu/awardmontanafaq.html#scholarship_waiver_faq)

IMPORTANT - PLEASE NOTE:

_Information regarding scholarships awarded by our office is subject to change based_
_on final budget approvals. Funding for these scholarships is not guaranteed and final_
_approval for scholarship awards may be determined after the application period has_
_ended._

_In addition, criteria noted for each scholarship is used as a minimum starting point_
_for consideration, the final number of scholarships may be limited. Meeting the eligibility_
_criteria does not guarantee selection._

**MUSHS APPLICATIONS WILL OPEN DECEMBER 1, 2026**

**MUSHS APPLICATIONS ARE DUE MARCH 15, 2027**

[Apply Now, or Manage an Existing Award](https://oche.my.site.com/)

[Recipient-list link omitted; not accessed]

### **Student Eligibility Requirements**

To apply students must:

- Must apply the year they graduate from a high school accredited by the Montana Board
of Public Education [list of eligible schools](https://mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Scholarships/_MT%20High%20schools%20accredited%20by%20MT%20Board%20of%20Public%20Ed.pdf)
- Must have been enrolled full-time at a high school accredited by the Montana Board
of Public Education for at least three years (any combination of three years but must
include senior year)
- Must have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.4 at the end of the 7th semester
- Must be on track to meet the [Board of Regents Rigorous Core Requirements](https://mus.edu/Prepare/docs/Rigorous-Core-Fact-Sheet.pdf) OR receive an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma by graduation
- Must take the ACT or SAT test by February of the year the student graduates
- Must be a [resident of the State of Montana](https://mus.edu/borpol/bor900/940-1.pdf)
- Must be accepted by an eligible campus

### **MUS Honor Scholarships may be used at the following campuses:**

U of M - Missoula

Missoula College UM

Bitterroot College

U of M - Western

Helena College UM

Montana Technological Universtiy

Highlands College of MT Tech

MSU - Bozeman

Gallatin College

MSU - Billings

City College MSU

MSU - Northern

Great Falls College MSU

Dawson CC

Flathead CC

Miles CC

### **Application Process**

Applying for the MUS Honor Scholarship is a multi-step process. Students must complete
each of the following steps by the **March 15th** deadline for their application to be considered complete;

      1\. Take the ACT or SAT test by February 2027

      2\. Apply to and be accepted by one of the eligible campuses

      3\. Apply online [AwardMontana.mus.edu](https://awardmontana.mus.edu/) (applications open December 1)

      4\. Print the Rigorous Core/IB/Attendance Certification page from your application,
have your High School                            Counselor/Designee sign it

**ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTS THAT MUST BE UPLOADED TO COMPLETE THE APPLICATION IN THE PORTAL**

- Copy of official 7th semester transcript reflecting all classes from freshman through
the first semester of senior year and cumulative GPA. To count Algebra I taken in
middle school to meet the Rigorous Core Requirements, students must also upload their
middle school transcript, ALL other courses must be reflected on their high school
transcript
- Copy of College Acceptance Letter or Acceptance email
- Proof/certification of ACT/SAT score taken by February 2027 (print out from ACT/SAT
OR listed as part of high school transcript)  Students can submit ACT Superscores,
as long as they only include tests taken by February the year they graduate
- Rigorous Core/IB/Attendance Certification page, signed by your High School Counselor/Designee

### **How are the scholarships awarded?**

Students from each high school will be ranked in GPA order. The individual(s) with
the highest GPA will be awarded 30 points, the next highest will be given 29, and
so forth, until all students with at least a 3.4 GPA are ranked. Once the GPA score
has been determined, this score will be added to the student’s ACT or SAT\* score (taken
by February the year they graduate\*\*), whichever is higher, to create a composite
score. The students with the highest composite scores in the state will be offered
the MUS Honor Scholarship.

\*SAT scores are converted to equivalent ACT scores

\*\*Students can submit ACT Superscores, as long as they only include tests taken by
February of the year they graduate

**UN-WEIGHTED example GPA Ranking For MUSHS Scoring Purposes**(GPAs will be rounded to the nearest tenth)

**WEIGHTED example GPA Ranking For MUSHS Scoring Purposes**(GPAs will be rounded to the nearest tenth)

[Illustrative student GPA tables omitted]

A high school which uses weighted grade point averages must use weighted averages
for all students.

### **Scholarship Award Process**

- Once awards are announced (early- to mid-April) High School Counselors/Designees will
be notified, in addition, **ALL** recipients of these scholarships will be notified by email.
- If awarded, each recipient must accept or decline the offered scholarship, please
be sure to return the information promptly.

### **Scholarship Retention**

This scholarship may be retained for a maximum of 8 semesters. Students must:

1. Utilize the scholarship within 9 months after high school graduation;
2. Maintain a 3.4 cumulative grade point average (GPA) per academic year;
3. **Complete a minimum of 30 credits after two semesters, 60 credit hours after four semesters,**
**and 90 credit hours after six semesters**;
4. Abide by the student conduct code of the home campus; and
5. Remain enrolled full-time (12+ credits) continuously each fall/spring semester for
    the life of the scholarship.

### **Transferring MUS Honor Scholarships**

With proper notification, MUS Scholarships may be transferred to other eligible campuses.
Please sign into the Award Montana Portal to fill in the Campus Change form on the
top tab

[Request a Campus Change](https://oche.my.site.com/)

Are you a dedicated student referee who balances the demands of academic life with the responsibilities of officiating in sports? Your commitment to fairness, leadership, and teamwork does not go unnoticed. The Student Referee Scholarship , we believe in recognizing and supporting individuals like you who contribute significantly to both their communities and their educational pursuits.

This scholarship is designed to reward exceptional student referees who exemplify integrity, dedication, and a passion for sportsmanship. We invite you to apply for the Student Referee Scholarship and share your journey as a student referee. Your unique perspective and dedication are what we seek to honor, and we are excited to support your continued growth and success both on and off the field.

**2027 Scholarship Dates**

Welcome to the The Student Referee Scholarship for High School Student Referees enrolled in a state accredited sports officiating class or currently officiating games in their community.

Scholarship amounts are $500 (multiple scholarships to be awarded, dependent on donations)

Are you a dedicated student referee who balances the demands of academic life with the responsibilities of officiating in sports? Your commitment to fairness, leadership, and teamwork does not go unnoticed. The Student Referee Scholarship , we believe in recognizing and supporting individuals like you who contribute significantly to both their communities and their educational pursuits.

This scholarship is designed to reward exceptional student referees who exemplify integrity, dedication, and a passion for sportsmanship. By providing financial assistance, we aim to support your academic goals and celebrate the invaluable role you play in promoting positive athletic experiences. Whether you’re officiating a local game or leading a major tournament, your efforts make a meaningful difference.

We invite you to apply for the Student Referee Scholarship and share your journey as a student referee. Your unique perspective and dedication are what we seek to honor, and we are excited to support your continued growth and success both on and off the field.

# BigSun Scholarship...2027

The BigSun Organization is proud to be able to help young athletes succeed in their academic pursuits. In order to do our part we are offering an annual scholarship to a deserving student. All student athletes are eligible regardless of the sport they are engaged in or the capacity in which they participate. The student must be a high school senior or be attending a post secondary institute.

Amount of Scholarship

The individual award is $500

## How to Apply

### WARNING - AI generated essays will not be accepted.

### Please send us a short essay (500 - 1,000 words) answering the following questions:

- How did your participation in sports during your high school years influence you?
- Has your participation influenced your career goals?
- Has your participation influenced how you relate to your family?

[Deadline](https://bigsunathletics.com/#collapseOne)

#### June 19, 2027.

[Who is eligible?](https://bigsunathletics.com/#collapseTwo)

All student athletes are eligible regardless of the sport they are engaged in or the capacity in which they participate. The student must be a high school senior or be attending a post secondary institute.

Please remember to include your name and the name of the school that you are attending.

[How to submit](https://bigsunathletics.com/#collapseThree)

All essay submissions should be sent to: **_"[contact redacted]"_**

[When is the winner notified?](https://bigsunathletics.com/#collapseFour)

The winner will be notified within 2 weeks of the deadline and the name of the winner will be posted on this website at that time.

[When is the award received?](https://bigsunathletics.com/#collapseFive)

The award is mailed within 2 weeks of the deadline.


**##### Number of Awards**

**The number of awards will vary each year and this is at the sole discretion of the scholarship award committee.**
